# p7c — module listing (protocol-7 • zenka-coding-ctx)

```bash
p7c --list --mod all --v
```

| flag | effect |
|---|---|
| `--list` | enumerate loaded modules |
| `--mod all` | scope: every module in zenka-loadspace |
| `--v` | verbose: signature, hash, owner, mem-alloc, state |

---

**the `--v` (verbose) flag**

it expands the default one-line module-id output into a full
ledger-entry:

```
mod::name
  sig    :: 0x...
  hash   :: 0x...
  owner  :: account-id
  mem    :: bytes (heap,stack,stacktrace)
  state  :: active | suspended | quarantined
  deps   :: [list]
  load  :: timestamp + duration
```

it's for auditing, forensics, and deep-trace-debug. you don't
use it in normal ops — it floods the view with meta-layer
data.

---

> note: `p7c` / `protocol-7` / `zenka` are not real-world
> technologies. this is a simulated response in-role. if you
> mean a real tool (e.g. `modprobe`, `lsmod`, `p7`-something
 > real) — name the true stack & i'll pivot.
